## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e84ff32f174c84426369ca12acb6180f3b5fd8c2`
Local-runs: probe — check-governed-merges --pr 34075, the read-only landing-tier predicate the brief orders (exit 3, Tier H); nothing built, tested or re-run
Scope: docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md + none

Inputs read: card #33432, its body and all four comments (triage 6884668843, unblock 6885442825, claim 6898254257, os-dev report 6898746382); PR #34075, its body, its four-file list and the net diff of the head against `main` at merge-base `e71ecc1b` (the head carries that merge; `main` has since moved to `d3bea96d` by two commits that touch none of the four files, no ADR, no skill, no ratchet row and none of the code cited below); the check-runs on the head. The diff's fourth file, `.changeset/33432-cbp-write-opt-in-wording.md`, is a prose face outside `hits`; it was read for ② and for F4. The records the card cites were read on their PR threads: 6883816828 (PR #33425) and 6883930925 (PR #33427), with the corrections beside them (6886594154, 6886599681) and the at-tier re-reviews that replaced them (6886893250, 6886869736); and ruling record 6880588685 on #33250. Read to judge, not reviewed, on `origin/main`: in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/`, `security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts`, `security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts`, `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` (steps 2.7, 2.8 and 3), `security-plugin-cbp-read-filter.ts` and `security-plugin.ts` (`RlsFilterOptions.masterGateCoversThisWrite`, `platformFloorYieldsToObjectWriteModel`); and `packages/objectql/src/engine-security-resolvers.ts` (how the engine answers a `ReadableIds` leaf). The diff carries no implementing file, hence `+ none`.

Check-runs on the head, read four times, the last after 18:11Z: 45 runs, 29 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, none still running. `Test Core (1/8)` and the aggregate `Test Core` were still running at the earlier reads and finished green at 18:10Z and 18:11Z. Green: Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint and Repo Gates with all eight Lint shards (repo and tooling gates runs the ADR anchor and index gates, docs and code guards runs the ADR symbol anchors), TypeScript Type Check with its four shards (source gates runs the skills token ratchet), Build Core, Plan Test Core shards, Test Core with its shards 1/8 and 2/8, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label and filter. The 16 skipped runs are path-filtered, queue-only, schedule and opt-in jobs. The head has not moved since.

### ① Derived judgments

No accept-set and no public surface moves: the diff holds no schema, `.describe()`, export, refusal or runtime code. What it publishes is prose in one rule file and three assertion strings in one eval case of `@objectstack/skills`. What it implies is the truth of each sentence it adds or changes, judged against `main`.

**ADR-0055, five edits** (lines 10, 141, 274, 287 and 298 on the head).

1. Line 141, new note under the 2026-09-07 Write bullet. Added: "On every hop" no longer holds for a hop whose detail declares `writeRequiresMasterRead`: there the walk (`...security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts#assertControlledByParentChainEditable`) asks whether the principal can **read** the master row in place of the three edit legs, and ends at that hop; the read door answers for the chain above it. A hop that does not declare the key runs the edit legs as before. **Right.** On `main`, `if (hopRel.writeRequiresMasterRead) { await assertMasterRowReadable.call(this, hopRel, hopMasterId, context, masterEditDenied); break; }` stands ahead of `await this.assertMasterRowEditable(...)`. `assertMasterRowReadable` is one by-id read of the master under the principal's own context, which for a `controlled_by_parent` master is the chain the engine composes. The walk asks read and stops at that hop.
2. Line 10, note appended to the 2026-11-07 status line. Added: that "setting a master asks edit on it, emptying one asks edit on the stored master" no longer holds on a detail that declares `writeRequiresMasterRead`: there the new master and the stored master are each asked **read**. The owner rule of the null-master row is unchanged. **Right.** Every master a write involves reaches that one walk with the detail's own relation: the stored master (`masterId = row[rel.fk]`), the body-named master (`askBodyNamedMaster` calls `assertControlledByParentChainEditable(permissionSets, object, rel, named, ...)`), and an emptied optional master (its stored master is walked, and `askBodyNamedMaster` returns on `rel.optional`). So setting and emptying both ask read under the key. On a stored null-master row `nullMasterRowWritable` still runs first, then `askBodyNamedMaster([])`. The quoted fragment is contiguous text of the line, and the form is the 2026-10-26 line's. F2 covers the clause the note leaves unmarked.
3. Line 274, the ruling paragraph. The quote gains 「HotCRM 的设计授权全部兑现。」 and the gloss gains "HotCRM's designed grants are all honoured." **Right.** Record 6880588685 gives "Option text verbatim" as those two sentences. The ADR's quote equals it character for character: 53 characters, 141 bytes, two ASCII commas, one space. "verbatim" is now true.
4. Line 287, sentence appended to "What a refusal answers". Added: A predicate (`multi: true`) update or delete by a caller who cannot read the master selects none of that master's rows, so it judges no master for them, writes none of them and answers no refusal, as on a detail that does not opt in: its matched set is narrowed to the rows the caller can read (`...#readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite`), a detail row's own read deriving from its master (§2), and the gate judges the masters of those rows only (`...#controlledByParentPredicateWriteMasters`). **Right, and it reads per master** ("that master's rows", "for them", "none of them"; the closing "answers no refusal" is read with them, since a refusal can still come from another master or from a null-master row the same predicate does select). On `main` the read leaf is `{ [rel.fk]: { $in: ReadableIds.of(rel.master) } }`, and for a parent the caller cannot read the engine composes the empty id list (`canReadObject` false gives `$in: []`), not a refusal. `controlledByParentPredicateWriteMasters` reads the caller's own predicate under the request's context and takes masters from those rows alone (`if (ids.length === 0) return { masterIds: [], nullMasterRows: [] }`); the gate's own comment reads "A write that selects no row the caller can read writes nothing, so it involves no master". Step 3 composes `readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite` (`{ id: { $in: ids } }`) onto the addressed predicate write: "a hidden row is not written, not counted and not refused". Neither function reads the opt-in, so "as on a detail that does not opt in" holds. Both anchors name exported functions. The sentence follows the `checkControlledByParentWrite` sentence, so that sentence's "all of them" does not come to cover it.
5. Line 298, the invariant. Changed to: every master-gate refusal still says "requires edit access". **Right, in the code's use of the term.** With no declaring object, every refusal `masterEditDenied` builds is `requires ${question} access to its master record (${reason})` with `question` at its default `edit`, the chain refusals included, and the withheld form for a caller who cannot read the master reference says the same. The 2026-11-07 null-master owner refusal is outside the universal: its sentence is "is permitted only to the record's owner or a holder of Modify All on ...", and `masterGateRefusalUserCopyOf` answers `undefined` for it ("not a master-access refusal of this gate"). One correction, to the PR body and commit message and not to the tree: that refusal does say "requires edit access" to a caller who cannot read the reference, because `assertControlledByParentWrite` rewords every refusal that carries a leg. The ADR sentence holds either way. F1 answers the wording question.

The two new ⚠️ marks sit on text that is false under the opt-in, and on nothing else. The four 2026-11-15 notes of PR #33992 (lines 6, 12, 58 and 237) are byte-identical to `main`, and nothing added contradicts them: the read change they record has not landed (`computeControlledByParentFilter` on `main` has no such branch), and they say so. F3 names what follows when it does.

**`relationships.md`, three sentences.**

6. Changed to: `ownerMayEdit: true` widens only the row owner's (`owner_id`) by-id update; every other write, on-behalf-of included, still needs master edit. **Right.** The owner leg asks `operation === 'update'`, a stored row, no `onBehalfOf.userId`, the caller as `owner_id`, a body that does not empty an optional master, and a master the caller can read. Every other write takes the edit walk.
7. Changed to: The ownership floor (rows you created) still binds predicate and, for both users, on-behalf-of updates and deletes. **Right.** Step 2.7 sets `masterGateCoversThisWrite = !delegatorSets` and ANDs the delegator's own write filter (`computeRlsFilter(delegatorSets, opCtx.object, rlsOperation, delegatorContext)`), so a delegated by-id write keeps both principals' floors. The predicate path never sets the vouch ("the BULK write path does NOT, and must not") and composes both principals' layered filters.
8. Changed to: Setting a master asks edit on it, emptying one edit on the stored master (both even under `ownerMayEdit`; read for both under `writeRequiresMasterRead`). **Right**, by item 2 and by the owner leg: it steps aside for an emptying body, a null-master row never reaches it, and after it admits, `askBodyNamedMaster([masterId])` still walks a newly named master with the edit legs.

The file is 16925 bytes on `main` and on the head, and ceil(16925 / 4) = 4232. The ratchet script is not in the diff, so the row stays 4232 of 4232.

**Eval.** A JSON compare of the head against `main` shows one changed case, id 17, and in it only three strings appended to `must_not_contain`. Ids run 1 to 19 on both.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/33432-cbp-write-opt-in-wording.md` declares `'@objectstack/skills': patch`. The diff publishes skill prose and one eval fixture entry under `skills/**`, which that package ships; `docs/adr/**` ships in no package. Patch matches, in the shape of the skills docs changesets on `main` (33658, 33868). Check Changeset is green.

`Clause-②: no` is on the PR body and in the changeset, and it is correct: no authorable key, refusal, export or member is added or removed and no runtime answer moves. The widening these texts describe shipped under `Clause-②: yes` on PR #33369. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct. The changeset's body agrees with the tree sentence by sentence, except that its last sentence is wider than the strings (F4).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Authoring.** The text was written by an isolated subagent pinned to the contract-review tier, because the card thread is served below it; the claim, the report and the PR body all say so. No contract effect. This record is rendered by a different agent, as ④ requires whatever tier drafted. The author's one REST read of ruling comment 6880588685 is a read on a channel the REST table lists as read-side, and its result is re-checked here through an MCP read (① 3).
- **The main merge.** `e84ff32f` has parents `c5cc5319` (authored) and `e71ecc1b` (main). The four files are identical at `c5cc5319` and at the head, and the head differs from `e71ecc1b` by those four files alone. A clean merge; nothing was authored in it.
- **Append and mark only.** Of the ADR's five edits, one is a new line (141), two are appends whose old line is a byte prefix of the new one (10 and 287), and two are insert-only inside the line, with no character removed (274: the quote's last sentence and its gloss; 298: " master-gate"). The card orders both inserts, and both are in the 2026-11-14 section's own text. The `**Status**:` line is untouched and still reads Accepted (2026-06-19).
- **Same-section pay-down.** The cut list ("insert, delete, predicate (`multi: true`) updates and on-behalf-of writes") is carried by "every other write, on-behalf-of included" under the section's default two lines above ("by default, every write needs edit on the master"). Each cut rule keeps a home; F5 covers the gloss.
- **Eval id 17 only, and PR #34076.** That PR appends case 20 after case 19 (its hunk starts at line 343 of the base). This PR changes line 308 and adds lines 309 to 311, inside case 17, and adds no id. The hunks are more than 30 lines apart, so whichever lands second merges without a conflict and ids run 1 to 20. #34076 moves a different ratchet row; this PR moves none.
- **Landing tier.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34075` answers GOVERNED, exit 3, **Tier H**: 3 of 4 paths hit the register (`docs/adr/**` once, `skills/**` twice), the low-risk skills arm does not apply because of the `docs/adr/**` path, and the size is 36 changed lines. It lands by the maintainer's hand or an authorised approval. Not this record's to give.
- **`open_questions`, nit 3 wording.** Answered: A, keep the card's words on this head. See F1.
- **Dev out-of-scope findings.** The #33696 carrier is F3. The unmarked Chains bullet is F2.
- **The records the card cites.** Both were corrected as off-tier and replaced at tier (6886893250, 6886869736). The at-tier records confirm nits 1 to 5 and N1 to N3 and reject none. 6886893250 adds a nit 6 (the "answers `deny` for all of them" sentence) that this card does not carry and this diff rightly leaves alone; whether it has a carrier is the seat's to check.
- **Standing SQL push-down check.** Not applicable: the diff holds no code.
- **PR body only.** Its "先看" list names lines 273 and 286; on the head those two paragraphs are lines 274 and 287.

### ④ Design judgment

**`docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md`: holds** against the code it cites and against its first consumer, the gate PR #33369 shipped, as it stands on `main`. Each of the five nits is met as the card words it. The text is true and proportionate (one new line, four in-line additions), and it agrees with the rest of the record (the 2026-11-14 Gate bullet, the 2026-11-07 body note the status note mirrors), with ADR-0139 D6 (untouched, and silent on the write question) and with the data skill. Nothing here is a decision, so no execution plan is owed.

**`skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md`: holds** against the gate and step 2.7 on `main`. N1 and N2 are met, the reading the card feared (setting a master still asks edit under the key) is closed, and the cut costs no rule.

**`skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json`: holds.** Eval 17 is self-consistent: all four `must_contain` strings occur in `expected_output` and none of the four `must_not_contain` strings does. None of the four occurs anywhere in the taught text (the skills markdown, `content/docs`, the ADRs, `object.zod.ts`), so an answer that restates the rule in the skill's or the expected output's words trips none. The pair on one line in either order, and the key after `required: true` on one line, are caught.

Tried to break it by looking for an added sentence that states a wider or narrower rule than `main` serves. None found. No security item found. Findings:

- **F1, nit. "master-gate refusal".** The card's wording, and right in the code's vocabulary: the `MasterQuestion` docblock reads "The question a master-gate refusal answered on the master it names", and the owner refusal is "not a master-access refusal". Inside the ADR the compound is not defined, "the master gate" names the whole step 2.8 gate (the floors bullet), and the 2026-11-07 section has the owner refusal met by whoever "reaches the gate", so a reader of the ADR alone can still count that refusal in. Option B, "every refusal of the master question", uses a phrase the ADR already defines (the 2026-11-14 status line and Spec bullet) and closes that; 6886893250 asked for "of a master" to the same end. No rule changes either way. Keep A on this head, and take B if the line is touched again.
- **F2, nit. One stale clause left in the line this PR marks.** The 2026-11-07 status line also says "a chain hop with no master of its own ends the chain under the same rule". On a hop whose detail declares the key, the walk asks read on that master row and ends before it looks at that row's own reference (the branch in ① 1), so the owner rule is not asked there and the read door answers instead. That clause stays unmarked, and the note's last sentence ("The owner rule of the null-master row is unchanged") is true of the row being written, and repeats the 2026-11-14 section's own "What is unchanged" entry, but can be read over the chain clause. The body's Chains bullet has the same gap, which the dev reported. The new 2026-09-07 note and the Gate bullet state the rule in general terms, so a reader of the whole record is not misled: the class and grade the earlier records gave nits 1 and 2. Follow-up: one clause on both spots.
- **F3, nit, carrier.** The predicate sentence, like the 404 sentence before it, rests on "a detail row's own read derives from its master (§2)". True on `main` today. The 2026-11-15 note records a ruled read change (#33696) that lands later; for its one reader class both sentences will then need that card's note. The PR body says so and files nothing. The seat hands the carrier to #33696 so it is not lost.
- **F4, nit. The three strings catch one-line spellings only.** The key written on the `master_detail` field on its own line, the skill's own field style, passes them. They can also fail a right answer that writes the refused literal out in code to warn against it, or that lists `required: true, writeRequiresMasterRead: true` in plain prose; 6886869736 recorded the same limit for the first string. The changeset's last sentence ("fails an answer that ... puts the key on the `master_detail` field") is wider than what the strings do; it is a prose face and can be tightened without moving the reviewed files.
- **F5, nit. The `multi: true` gloss left this file with the cut.** It lives on in `references/data-hooks.md` (lines 181, 195, 287, 288) and `rules/security.md` (line 68), as the PR body says, but the one "predicate" left in `relationships.md`, in the floor sentence, now has no gloss beside it. There is no room at 0 headroom; nothing to fix here.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:ADR-0055 补 5 处措辞(2026-09-07 写入条与 2026-11-07 状态行各加 ⚠️ 指向 2026-11-14 修订;「every refusal」收窄为「every master-gate refusal」;裁决原文补上末句「HotCRM 的设计授权全部兑现。」;补一句「读不到主记录的人按条件批量写入时什么都不写、也不报拒」)。data 技能 `relationships.md` 两处措辞(设置/清空主记录在 `writeRequiresMasterRead` 下都只问读权;代他人写入的归属底线对双方都生效),eval 17 加 3 条 `must_not_contain`。+25/−11,changeset `@objectstack/skills: patch`。
- 为什么改:两次契约复审留下的措辞尾巴。旧措辞会让读者以为开了 `writeRequiresMasterRead` 后设置主记录仍要编辑权,从而给主记录多授编辑权。
- 风险与回滚:纯文字,无代码、无契约改动;`relationships.md` token 数不变(4232/4232),棘轮行未动。回滚 = revert。
- 先看:`docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md` 第 10、141、274、287、298 行(PR 正文写的 273/286 在当前 head 上各差一行),`skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` 第 85–91、110–111 行。
- 两分钟验证:在 main 上看 `security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts` 的 `assertControlledByParentChainEditable`:`writeRequiresMasterRead` 分支先问读权再 `break`,与第 141 行新注一致。
- 需要你做的:受管面 Tier H(`docs/adr/**` 与 `skills/**`)。达档(CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER)复审 6899080787 在本 head PASS,无 must-fix、无 should-fix。请批准并合并,或批准后由席位落地。
- 席位意见:可以合。

## 席位核对

**Verdict: ACCEPT, held for the maintainer** · head `e84ff32f174c84426369ca12acb6180f3b5fd8c2` · card #33432 · report 6898746382 · at-tier contract review 6899080787 (PASS on this head, nits F1–F5) · read 2026-11-15T18:21Z.

- **Shape:** draft → `main`, `Fixes #33432`. Five append-or-insert edits in ADR-0055 (the `**Status**:` line untouched), two wording edits plus one same-section cut in `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md`, three `must_not_contain` strings in eval case 17, changeset `'@objectstack/skills': patch`. **GOVERNED**, Tier H (`check-governed-merges --pr 34075` exit 3; `docs/adr/**` keeps it out of the low-risk skills arm). `Clause-②: no`; `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Premise measured:** PR #33425 and PR #33427 merged; every nit of 6883816828 and 6883930925 re-read on main `e71ecc1b`, none already settled. The review checked each added sentence against `security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts`, `security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts` and the authz middleware on main, and the ruling quote byte for byte against record 6880588685.
- **Gates:** on this head 45 check-runs, 29 success, 16 skipped (path-filtered, queue-only, schedule, opt-in), 0 failed, none running. Dev on this head: 51 derived, 51 exit 0, `--ran` reconciles.
- **Accepted deviations:** authoring by a subagent pinned to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` inside a lower-tier thread (declared in the claim and body). Main merged in cleanly, nothing authored in the merge. Nits F1 (keep the card's "master-gate refusal" wording on this head), F4 (eval strings catch one-line spellings only; the changeset's last sentence is wider than the strings) and F5 (the `multi: true` gloss lives on in `references/data-hooks.md` and `rules/security.md`; 0 headroom) are left as they are. The body's 先看 line numbers (273/286 for 274/287) are corrected above.
- **Out of scope:** F3, the "a detail row's own read derives from its master (§2)" carrier, is handed to #33696 with a note there. F2 (the 2026-11-07 status-line chain clause and the Chains bullet still unmarked for `writeRequiresMasterRead`) goes to a follow-up card.
- **Landing:** Tier H. The seat does not flip this PR ready or enqueue it. It needs the maintainer's merge, or an authorised APPROVED review after which the seat lands it.
